title: In five primate alignments, insertions between closely spaced conserved non-coding blocks are rarer than at one-sided block edges, and indel lengths show no DNA helical-phase pattern
abstract:
In conserved human non-coding DNA, insertions that add DNA between two nearby conserved blocks are rare, and more so the closer the blocks are, while insertions next to a block but not between two blocks are much less rare; indel lengths show no preference for multiples of the DNA helical repeat (about 10.5 bp). This matters because substitution-based conservation scores do not measure length constraint, and a common model of gene control says binding sites must face the same side of the helix.

I compared human with chimpanzee, gorilla, orangutan, macaque and marmoset alignments (52.2 million insertion and deletion events, indels). For each DNA class and indel length (1-60 bp), I divided observed indels by the number expected from a reference class with the same GC content, homopolymer context and transposon status (O/E), with bootstrap intervals over 10-Mb genome blocks.

At the same distance (1 bp) from the nearest conserved block, insertions of 3-60 bp had O/E relative to one-sided block edges of 0.59 [0.57, 0.62] when the two blocks were at most 10 bp apart, 0.72 for 11-30 bp, 0.82 for 31-100 bp and 0.94 for 101-300 bp, in this order in each species. Edges of blocks with another block within 30 bp on their far side showed a much weaker deficit (0.94 [0.88, 1.00]; per species 0.92-1.11), so most of the deficit belongs to DNA between blocks, not to conserved clusters.

Positive controls worked: protein-coding DNA showed the 3-bp reading-frame signal (periodic coefficient a = 1.16 [1.13, 1.20]) and 5' untranslated regions a weaker one (a = 0.114). For conserved non-coding DNA the pre-specified 10.5-bp coefficient was negative (a = -0.025 [-0.031, -0.018]), but its size is typical of non-helical periods and the periodogram peaks are at 6-8 bp. In gaps between conserved blocks, helical-phase purging has a depth of at most 2-4% of half-turn indels, about one fifth of the frame effect in 5' untranslated regions. Non-conserved DNA in ENCODE enhancer-like elements had no detectable indel deficit (O/E 1.04; low sensitivity).

Limits: alignments can misplace indels; phastCons borders come from substitutions in the same primates, so gap DNA may also carry weak sequence constraint; evidence is comparative. Prediction for reporter assays: 3-10 bp insertions into non-conserved gaps of 10 bp or less between conserved blocks reduce enhancer activity more than the same insertions just outside a block, and 10-bp insertions are not better tolerated than 5-bp ones.

display.caption: Spacing constraint between conserved blocks (human vs five primates). A: Insertions placed strictly between two conserved blocks, observed/expected relative to one-sided block edges, by insertion length and gap size (corrected for junction opportunity; not distance-matched). Dashed: insertions inside conserved blocks. B: At 1 bp from the nearest block, insertion O/E (3-60 bp, blue; 1-2 bp, green) falls as the two blocks get closer, while substitution O/E (orange) stays at 0.90-0.93. Control (separate reference: edges of isolated blocks): edges of blocks with another block within 30 bp on the far side show a much weaker deficit. Bars: 95% bootstrap intervals over 10-Mb genome blocks.

No helical-phase signal. Left: periodograms of the indel length ratio against a smooth trend; dashed line: simulated white-noise 95% null for the maximum (too permissive for conserved DNA); shaded band: DNA helical repeat (10-11 bp). Coding DNA and 5' UTRs peak at 3 bp; conserved non-coding classes peak at 6-8 bp. Right: periodic coefficients a with block-bootstrap (thick) and length-level quasi-Poisson (thin) 95% intervals. Coefficients at arbitrary non-helical periods vary about as much as a(10.5) in conserved DNA; see README for revised bounds.

Indel length spectra relative to context-matched neutral DNA (human vs five primates). A, B: Protein-coding DNA and 5' UTRs favour lengths that are multiples of 3 (blue). C: Conserved non-coding DNA (phastCons elements and gaps of 100 bp or less between them). D: Gaps between conserved blocks (non-repeat, isolated indels). In C and D, lengths within 1 bp of a multiple of 10.5 bp (blue) do not lie above the smooth trend. Bars: Poisson 95% intervals.

citations.reason: Indel-based detection of functional DNA independent of substitutions, including sequence under heterogeneous selection; closest prior work on length constraint. This study places such constraint between nearby conserved blocks and tests helical phase.
Indel-based estimate of the constrained fraction of the human genome (8.2%).
Reported depletion of non-multiple-of-three indels in mammalian 5' UTRs; reproduced here as a positive control.
phastCons conserved elements define the conserved blocks and spacers.
ENCODE candidate cis-regulatory elements (registry v4) used as annotation.
Reported a 10.5-bp helical spacing preference in learned motif syntax; motivates the helical-phase test.
Natural indels that change spacing between transcription-factor pairs are mostly tolerated at the level of binding and acetylation; consistent with spacing constraint concentrated in very short gaps.
Reporter assays support a flexible regulatory grammar; consistent with no helical-phase signal.
Indel mutation-rate heterogeneity can mimic selection; motivates the context matching and artifact checks.
Simulated spacer-length distortion by indels in binding-site evolution.
Nucleosome-linked 10-bp mutation periodicity; a possible source of periodic mutation spectra.
IFN-beta enhanceosome, a classic case of helical-phase dependence, cited as a known exception.
UCSC hg38 pairwise net alignments to five primates and annotation tables.
Length constraint on enhancer-to-gene distances (kilobase scale); this study adds the 1-60 bp scale.
Natural deletions between genes and enhancers; spacing at a larger scale.
Length constraint on introns of immediate-early genes.
Little selection on regulatory elements without mammal conservation; consistent with no indel deficit in non-conserved cCRE DNA here.
Weak amino-acid selection on ncORFs; consistent with no frame signal in lncRNA exons here.
